goal_checks.notes: Presence comes only from the live channel's own state (presenceToPeers over presenceState()); a departure removes the entry, and a dropped channel clears the peer list, so it self-cleans. live-channel.test.ts and use-presence.test.ts pin it.

peer-cursors is a canvas leaf with a painter (I17/I18/I25 green) fed by usePeerCursors: the container gets an imperative paint() and drives it from a ref, so no cursor value passes through useState; the send path is createThrottle(50) and only fires on real movement. throttle.test.ts and the peer-cursors tests pin both halves.

A teammate's highlight still re-renders through 007's path (broadcast-from-database -> applyRemote -> Dexie -> useLiveQuery); 015 adds no second render path and does not touch it. The private-highlight-on-no-shared-topic property remains task 002's proven result.

The leader indicator is raised by a cursor whose profileId is the leader's and whose page is current, is cleared by an explicit drawing:false frame (the stroke end), and has a 1.2s idle fallback. use-presence.test.ts proves the set and the clear, and that a non-leader/other-page cursor is ignored.

BLOCKED: the two-browser latency measurement (~100-300 ms) needs the live Supabase stack and two browsers; it cannot be performed by an agent. Nothing in test.json fabricates a latency number. The private-highlight routing half is already task 002's proof.

0006_live_topic.sql grants session members SELECT and INSERT on live:{sessionId} for broadcast + presence only; no INSERT policy exists on ws:/user: (0004 grants only SELECT there), so a member cannot insert a message on ws:{sessionId}. The policy mirrors 0004's proven shape; the live RLS confirmation is a follow-up (the SQL is deterministic).
